Either the kicker overclaims or the row understates; a skeptical reader sees the page contradict itself on the very rule it is built on.

findings.finding: Open question the manifest calls probe drift: in the --rm run, loading /#work leaves the page at y 0 (section top 7,710) in both the early and late read, so a visitor with the OS setting on may not land on a deep link. The default run's own reduced-motion rmHash passes at both widths (y 7,618, top 92) and pausedHash passes in the --rm run, so the same build reads both ways. The --rm context sets the preference from the first request, which is closer to a real OS-level user than a flip after load, so it should be treated as the more faithful reading until a manual repro clears it. A plausible mechanism (not verified): under RM the page leaves the jump to the browser (nav probe note), and streamed hidden blocks are not in the DOM at the moment the browser tries the fragment.
findings.evidence: probes-1440-rm layout-gates.rmHash (early/late y 0, top 7710) against probes-1440 and probes-1024 layout-gates.rmHash (y 7618, top 92); nav probe skipped under rm.
findings.action: Two-minute manual repro in a normal browser with prefers-reduced-motion on: open /#work, and /#kill-list. If it stays at the top, fix before release; if it lands, fix the probe's --rm path. The in-page 'Skip to the research' works under rm (jump.fastlane passes), so this is deep links only.
